primitives.verbatim_quote: Instead of that, what if we ranked every team's wide receivers and compared how each defense did against the opponent's number one playmaker?

primitives.breakdown_regime: When WR1 is eliminated, defensive EPA shifts toward non-WR1 targets.

primitives.name: Defensive Coverage Differential
primitives.verbatim_quote: Can we do better than just adding up the EPA from his swats and tackles, or just summarizing the defense as a whole?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ΔEPA': 'difference in expected points added, units: points', 'EPA_{WR1}': 'average EPA against top receiver, units: points', 'EPA_{non-WR1}': 'average EPA against other receivers, units: points'}
primitives.assumptions: EPA is additive and representative of coverage quality.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When ΔEPA is negative, defense underperforms against WR1.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that evaluating defensive performance requires isolating the impact of coverage on the top receiver versus aggregate performance. This is formalized through the WR1 Defensive Efficacy Index (DEI), which normalizes EPA against WR1 against all receivers. The Smittywerbenjagermenjensen Index (SWJ) acts as a selector function to isolate WR1 plays. The Defensive Coverage Differential (ΔEPA) then quantifies the strategic gap between defending the top threat and defending others. These operators form a dual structure: SWJ enables selection, while DEI and ΔEPA enable evaluation. Failure modes include misranking receivers due to sample size or confounding variables like weather or opponent strength. Temporal coherence is ensured by applying consistent receiver ranking criteria across seasons.
